quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A mid-sized music venue that had relied for years on touring national acts found those bookings increasingly unaffordable as larger competitors offered guarantees it could not match. Rather than abandoning live music, the owners created a residency program for emerging regional artists, offering a guaranteed monthly slot and a share of bar revenue instead of a flat fee. Several artists later credited the residency with building the local following that eventually let them tour nationally, and the venue's calendar is now booked nearly a year in advance.
options: A Venue That Stopped Hosting Live Music Entirely
Touring National Acts Becoming More Affordable Over Time
A Residency Program That Failed to Attract Bookings
A Residency Program Helping Both a Venue and Local Artists Thrive
quests.correctAnswer: A Residency Program Helping Both a Venue and Local Artists Thrive
quests.hint: Notice that the paragraph describes benefits to two different parties -- pay attention to how both the venue and the artists were affected by this new approach.
quests.explanation: Two connected outcomes make up the main idea here: the venue solved its booking problem, and the artists gained a launching pad for their own careers. The summary needs to capture that mutual benefit rather than focusing on only one side.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A city's 311 non-emergency service line had long been criticized for long hold times that discouraged residents from reporting issues like potholes or broken streetlights at all. After analyzing call data, officials discovered that a large share of calls involved a handful of repetitive, easily answered questions about trash pickup schedules. By building an automated voice menu to handle those specific questions upfront, the city freed human operators to address less routine issues faster, and overall resident satisfaction with the service rose even though total call volume stayed the same.
options: A City That Removed Its Non-Emergency Line Entirely
An Automated Menu Freeing Staff to Handle Complex Calls Faster
Call Volume That Decreased After the Automated Menu
Satisfaction That Dropped Despite the Same Call Volume
quests.correctAnswer: An Automated Menu Freeing Staff to Handle Complex Calls Faster
quests.hint: Consider what kind of calls were clogging the system and how separating those out changed how quickly other issues got handled.
quests.explanation: Identifying and automating routine questions frees up capacity for more complex ones here, improving overall satisfaction without reducing call volume. The summary should reflect that structural fix rather than a reduction in calls.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: For most of his adult life, Felix considered himself simply 'bad at cooking,' relying on takeout and frozen meals most nights. After a minor health scare prompted by his doctor's comments about his diet, he committed to learning just five simple recipes thoroughly rather than attempting a wide variety of dishes at once. Mastering this small, manageable set of meals built enough confidence that he gradually began experimenting with new ingredients and techniques on his own, eventually enjoying cooking as a hobby rather than viewing it as a chore he could not handle.
options: Mastering a Few Recipes Building Felix's Confidence to Cook More
Felix Continuing to Rely Entirely on Takeout
A Health Scare That Felix Chose to Ignore
Felix Attempting Many Difficult Recipes All at Once
quests.correctAnswer: Mastering a Few Recipes Building Felix's Confidence to Cook More
quests.hint: Think about the specific strategy Felix used, starting small, and how that approach led to a much bigger change in how he felt about cooking overall.
quests.explanation: A deliberate, limited starting point leads to broader confidence and a genuine change in attitude toward cooking. The summary should connect the small initial step with the larger transformation that followed, not just the health scare that prompted it.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A university's career services office had traditionally measured its own success by the number of students who attended job fairs and resume workshops, regardless of whether those students actually secured employment afterward. After shifting to track actual job placement rates instead, the office discovered that several of its most heavily attended programs had little measurable effect on whether students found jobs, while a less popular one-on-one coaching service correlated strongly with successful placements. Funding and staffing were subsequently redirected toward expanding the coaching service.
options: A University That Stopped Tracking Any Outcomes
The Most Popular Programs Proving Most Effective
New Metrics Revealing Which Career Program Actually Helped Students
Coaching Services That Were Defunded After the Change
quests.correctAnswer: New Metrics Revealing Which Career Program Actually Helped Students
quests.hint: Look at what the office used to measure versus what it measured after the change, and notice which kind of program the new measurement revealed to be truly effective.
quests.explanation: Switching from attendance to actual outcomes reveals a mismatch between popularity and effectiveness here. The summary should capture that the less-attended coaching service turned out to be more valuable, not the more popular ones.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A manufacturing plant's safety officer had assumed for years that most workplace injuries occurred during physically demanding tasks involving heavy machinery, and safety training resources were allocated accordingly. A detailed review of three years of incident reports revealed that the majority of injuries actually occurred during routine, low-risk tasks like walking between stations, often because workers were less alert during these perceived 'safe' moments. The plant redesigned its safety training to address complacency during routine tasks specifically, alongside its existing machinery training.
options: Data Revealing That Routine Tasks, Not Machinery, Caused Most Injuries
Heavy Machinery Confirmed as the Leading Cause of Injuries
A Plant That Removed All Machinery Safety Training
Workers Who Were Most Alert During Routine Tasks
quests.correctAnswer: Data Revealing That Routine Tasks, Not Machinery, Caused Most Injuries
quests.hint: Ask yourself what the safety officer originally assumed caused most injuries and what the actual data revealed instead.
quests.explanation: An assumption about where danger comes from is overturned here, showing routine tasks as the bigger hidden risk. The summary should reflect that surprising data finding rather than confirm the original assumption about machinery.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Cruise lines have traditionally marketed their largest ships by emphasizing the sheer number of onboard amenities, from multiple pools to elaborate theaters, assuming bigger always meant better value for travelers. Recent booking trends, however, show a growing segment of travelers actively choosing smaller ships with fewer amenities but more port time and fewer fellow passengers competing for excursions. Several major cruise lines have responded by expanding their smaller-ship offerings even as they continue building larger flagship vessels for a different segment of customers.
options: All Cruise Lines Abandoning Their Larger Ships
Travelers Universally Preferring Ships with More Amenities
Smaller Ships Disappearing from the Cruise Market
Some Travelers Choosing Smaller Ships Over Amenity-Packed Giants
quests.correctAnswer: Some Travelers Choosing Smaller Ships Over Amenity-Packed Giants
quests.hint: Identify the traditional assumption about ship size and amenities, then notice that the paragraph describes a specific, growing segment rather than every traveler.
quests.explanation: A meaningful but partial shift in preference is described here, not a complete industry change. The summary should reflect that a growing segment of travelers favors smaller ships, while larger ships still exist for other customers.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: When Theo and his sister inherited their childhood home after their mother's passing, neither initially wanted to sell it despite living in different states and rarely visiting in person. After a year of paying for upkeep on a house sitting empty most of the time, they finally agreed to convert it into a small vacation rental, splitting both the modest income and the periodic maintenance responsibilities. The arrangement let them preserve a place tied to their shared childhood memories without the financial burden of an unused property.
options: Theo and His Sister Selling the Home Immediately
Converting an Inherited Home into a Rental to Preserve It
A House That Remained Empty with No New Plan
Siblings Who Refused to Share Any Responsibilities
quests.correctAnswer: Converting an Inherited Home into a Rental to Preserve It
quests.hint: Focus on why the siblings did not want to sell and what compromise let them keep the home without the financial strain.
quests.explanation: A solution balancing emotional attachment with practical financial concerns is at the heart of this paragraph. The summary should capture that the rental arrangement preserved the home while solving the cost problem, not simply that they kept or sold it.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A regional department store chain that built its identity on offering deep discounts during frequent flash sales noticed that many loyal customers had grown to distrust the store's regular prices entirely, assuming everything was secretly marked up before each sale began. Customer surveys confirmed this suspicion was widespread, even though an internal audit showed prices were not artificially inflated beforehand. To rebuild trust, the chain published a public price history tool showing actual price changes over the previous year for any item.
options: An Audit That Confirmed Prices Were Artificially Inflated
Customers Who Fully Trusted the Store's Sale Pricing
A Price History Tool Addressing Customers' Distrust of Sale Pricing
A Chain That Removed All Flash Sales Permanently
quests.correctAnswer: A Price History Tool Addressing Customers' Distrust of Sale Pricing
quests.hint: Picture what customers suspected about the pricing, what the internal audit actually found, and what tool the chain created to address the gap between the two.
quests.explanation: A gap between customer perception and actual pricing practice gets addressed here through a transparency tool. The summary should connect the distrust with the specific solution rather than confirm the customers' suspicion was accurate.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Coffee shop owners in a competitive downtown district have generally assumed that customers choose where to buy coffee primarily based on taste and price, leading most shops to focus marketing efforts on bean quality and modest discounts. A local market research firm's survey instead found that consistency of wait time was the strongest predictor of customer loyalty in the area, often outweighing small differences in price or flavor. Several shops have since begun publicly posting estimated wait times to capitalize on this overlooked factor.
options: Taste and Price Confirmed as the Strongest Loyalty Factors
Wait Time Outweighing Taste and Price as the Real Loyalty Driver
Shops That Removed Wait Time Information from Customers
Customer Loyalty Found to Have No Predictable Cause
quests.correctAnswer: Wait Time Outweighing Taste and Price as the Real Loyalty Driver
quests.hint: Compare what shop owners traditionally assumed mattered most to customers with what the research actually identified as the strongest factor instead.
quests.explanation: A common assumption about taste and price gets challenged here, replaced by an overlooked factor the research identified. The summary should reflect that surprising finding about wait time rather than confirm the original assumption.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Smart home device manufacturers have generally assumed that customers want as many connected features as possible, packing thermostats, locks, and lighting systems with expanding functionality each year. A usability study following actual households for several months found that most users regularly engaged with only two or three core features, regardless of how many were available, and that excessive options often led to frustration during setup. Several manufacturers have since begun offering simplified 'essentials' versions of their products alongside their fully-featured originals.
options: Households Actively Using Every Available Feature
Manufacturers Removing All Simplified Product Options
A Study Finding No Connection Between Features and Frustration
A Study Finding Households Use Only a Few Smart Home Features
quests.correctAnswer: A Study Finding Households Use Only a Few Smart Home Features
quests.hint: Weigh what manufacturers assumed customers wanted against what the usability study actually found about how people use these devices in practice.
quests.explanation: An industry assumption about feature demand is contrasted here with research showing limited actual use. The summary should capture that gap and the resulting product change, not confirm the original assumption.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Physical therapists have traditionally measured recovery progress for knee injuries primarily through range-of-motion tests performed during clinic visits, assuming these brief snapshots accurately reflected a patient's overall functional improvement. Wearable sensor technology that tracks movement throughout a patient's entire day has revealed that some patients with excellent in-clinic range-of-motion scores were still avoiding using the injured knee normally during daily activities, masking lingering weakness that clinic-only assessments missed. Therapists using the sensor data have begun adjusting treatment plans to specifically address this avoidance behavior.
options: Sensor Data Revealing Hidden Weakness Behind Good Clinic Scores
Clinic Tests Confirmed as Fully Accurate Measures of Recovery
Patients Found to Have No Lingering Weakness at All
Therapists Who Refused to Adjust Treatment Based on New Data
quests.correctAnswer: Sensor Data Revealing Hidden Weakness Behind Good Clinic Scores
quests.hint: Notice what clinic-only tests were missing and what the all-day sensor data revealed that those brief tests could not show.
quests.explanation: A limitation in traditional in-clinic assessment gets exposed here by more continuous data. The summary should capture that hidden gap between test scores and real daily behavior, not confirm that clinic tests were sufficient.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Podcast networks have generally assumed that longer episodes signal more value to listeners, leading many shows to stretch content well past an hour even when the core material could be covered more briefly. Listener completion data from one major network revealed that episodes under forty minutes were finished at a noticeably higher rate than longer ones, regardless of topic or host popularity. Several shows on the network have since experimented with shorter formats, splitting previously single long episodes into two more focused parts.
options: Longer Episodes Confirmed to Have Higher Completion Rates
A Network That Increased All Episode Lengths Further
Listener Data Favoring Shorter Episodes Over Longer Ones
Episode Length Found to Have No Effect on Completion
quests.correctAnswer: Listener Data Favoring Shorter Episodes Over Longer Ones
quests.hint: Consider the assumption podcast networks made about episode length and what the actual listener completion data showed instead.
quests.explanation: An assumption that longer always means more valuable gets challenged here, with data favoring shorter episodes instead. The summary should reflect that finding rather than confirm the original assumption about length.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A government agency's official website had long presented benefit eligibility information across more than a dozen separate pages, each written by a different department using its own terminology, which frequently left applicants unsure whether they qualified for programs that might actually apply to them. After consolidating the information into a single eligibility questionnaire using consistent, plain-language terms throughout, the agency found that applications for previously underused programs rose substantially, suggesting that many eligible people had simply never realized they qualified.
options: An Agency That Removed All Eligibility Information
Applications That Declined After the Website Changes
Departments That Refused to Use Consistent Terminology
Plain-Language Consolidation Revealing Eligible People Who Never Applied
quests.correctAnswer: Plain-Language Consolidation Revealing Eligible People Who Never Applied
quests.hint: Think about the original problem with scattered, inconsistent information and what the rise in applications after consolidation suggests about who was missing out before.
quests.explanation: Confusing, fragmented information had been hiding real eligibility from potential applicants, and simplifying it reveals this hidden need. The summary should capture that underlying cause rather than just describe the website redesign.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Many people assume that multitasking allows them to accomplish more in less time, switching between several small tasks like emails, messages, and household chores throughout the day. A self-tracking experiment in which Lucia dedicated specific uninterrupted blocks of time to single tasks instead revealed that she actually completed the same total workload in noticeably less overall time, despite feeling like she was accomplishing less moment to moment compared to her usual scattered approach.
options: Single-Tasking Proving Faster Than Multitasking Despite Feeling Slower
Multitasking Confirmed as the More Efficient Approach
Lucia Completing Less Total Work with Time Blocking
An Experiment Showing No Difference Between the Two Approaches
quests.correctAnswer: Single-Tasking Proving Faster Than Multitasking Despite Feeling Slower
quests.hint: Look at the common belief about multitasking, then notice the gap between how Lucia felt moment to moment and what the actual results showed.
quests.explanation: A common assumption about multitasking is contrasted here with an experiment showing the opposite result, plus a gap between subjective feeling and actual outcome. The summary should capture that single-tasking was objectively faster despite feeling otherwise.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: School administrators evaluating a new reading intervention program initially focused only on standardized test score improvements, which showed modest but inconsistent gains across different schools. A closer look at qualitative teacher feedback, gathered separately, revealed the program's clearest benefit was actually increasing how much students voluntarily read for pleasure outside of class, a factor not captured by the standardized tests at all. Some districts have since begun tracking voluntary reading habits as a supplementary measure of the program's success.
options: Standardized Tests Capturing the Program's Full Benefit
Teacher Feedback Revealing a Benefit Standardized Tests Missed
A Program Found to Have No Measurable Benefits at All
Districts That Stopped Tracking Any Reading Habits
quests.correctAnswer: Teacher Feedback Revealing a Benefit Standardized Tests Missed
quests.hint: Ask yourself what the standardized test scores showed compared to what the teacher feedback revealed about a different kind of impact.
quests.explanation: A narrow measurement tool misses the program's most meaningful effect here, which only becomes visible through additional feedback. The summary should connect the qualitative finding with the gap left by the test scores alone.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: A remote-first software company that initially measured employee engagement primarily through meeting attendance and message response times found these metrics correlated poorly with actual project outcomes, since some highly responsive employees produced little finished work while some quieter employees consistently delivered strong results. After shifting performance reviews to focus on completed deliverables and peer feedback instead, several previously underrated employees received promotions, while a few highly visible but less productive employees faced difficult conversations about their actual output.
options: Responsiveness Confirmed as the Best Predictor of Output
A Company That Returned to Measuring Only Attendance
New Metrics Revealing a Mismatch Between Visibility and Output
Quiet Employees Found to Consistently Underperform
quests.correctAnswer: New Metrics Revealing a Mismatch Between Visibility and Output
quests.hint: Identify what the original metrics measured and how that compared to who actually produced strong results once the company looked more closely.
quests.explanation: Visible activity, like quick responses, does not reliably predict real output here, and switching measurement approaches surfaces previously overlooked strong performers. The summary should capture that mismatch and correction.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Travel insurance companies have traditionally priced policies primarily based on trip cost and destination, assuming these two factors were the strongest predictors of claims. A data analysis covering several years of claims, however, found that trip length was actually a stronger predictor of claim likelihood than destination, with longer trips of any kind showing disproportionately higher claim rates regardless of how exotic or routine the location was. Several insurers have begun adjusting their pricing models to weigh trip duration more heavily than before.
options: Destination Confirmed as the Strongest Predictor of Claims
Trip Length Found to Have No Effect on Claims
Claims Data Showing Trip Length Matters More Than Destination
Insurers Who Refused to Adjust Their Pricing Models
quests.correctAnswer: Claims Data Showing Trip Length Matters More Than Destination
quests.hint: Focus on which two factors insurers traditionally relied on and which factor the data actually showed mattered most.
quests.explanation: An assumption about destination being the key pricing factor is overturned here, replaced by trip length as the stronger predictor. The summary should reflect that specific data finding rather than confirm the original assumption.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Parenting advice has traditionally emphasized consistent daily routines as the foundation of a stable household, leading many parents to feel they were failing whenever unpredictable circumstances like illness or travel disrupted a carefully maintained schedule. A longitudinal study following families over several years found that children's sense of security correlated more strongly with predictable parental responses to disruption, such as calm reassurance during unexpected changes, than with the rigidity of the schedule itself. Researchers suggested this finding may ease unnecessary guilt among parents whose routines are frequently interrupted.
options: Strict Routines Confirmed as Essential for Child Security
Research Finding Parental Response Matters More Than Routine Rigidity
Parents Whose Routines Are Interrupted Found to Cause Lasting Harm
A Study Finding No Connection Between Parenting and Security
quests.correctAnswer: Research Finding Parental Response Matters More Than Routine Rigidity
quests.hint: Picture what parenting advice traditionally emphasized and what the study found actually mattered more for children's sense of security.
quests.explanation: A common emphasis on rigid routines gets challenged here, with parental response to disruption identified as the stronger factor. The summary should reflect that nuanced research finding rather than reinforce the original emphasis on strict schedules.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Online retailers have generally assumed that offering free shipping above a certain purchase threshold encourages customers to add more items to their cart, increasing overall order value. An analysis of purchasing behavior at one mid-sized retailer found that while customers did add items to reach the free shipping threshold, a significant portion of those added items were later returned, meaning the actual net revenue gain was much smaller than the gross order value suggested. The retailer adjusted its threshold strategy after factoring in these return patterns.
options: Return Patterns Undercutting the Real Benefit of Shipping Thresholds
Free Shipping Thresholds Confirmed to Boost Net Revenue Significantly
Customers Who Never Returned Any Added Items
A Retailer That Removed All Shipping Thresholds Immediately
quests.correctAnswer: Return Patterns Undercutting the Real Benefit of Shipping Thresholds
quests.hint: Compare the gross order value the threshold created with the actual net revenue once returns were factored in.
quests.explanation: An apparent benefit gets partially offset here by an overlooked factor: returns. The summary should capture that the real financial gain was smaller than it first appeared, not confirm the original assumption about increased revenue.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Nutrition labels in many countries have traditionally emphasized total calorie counts as the primary number consumers should consider when evaluating packaged food. Research following consumer behavior found that shoppers who were shown an additional 'minutes of walking needed to burn this' label alongside calorie counts chose lower-calorie options far more often than those shown calorie counts alone, suggesting that translating numbers into a relatable physical activity made the information more meaningful to everyday shoppers than the raw calorie figure by itself.
options: Calorie Counts Alone Found to Be Most Effective
Shoppers Who Ignored Both Types of Nutrition Labels
Activity-Based Labels Found to Confuse Most Shoppers
Activity-Based Labels Outperforming Raw Calorie Counts Alone
quests.correctAnswer: Activity-Based Labels Outperforming Raw Calorie Counts Alone
quests.hint: Weigh the two different labeling approaches the research compared and notice which one actually changed shoppers' choices more effectively.
quests.explanation: Two ways of presenting the same information are compared here, and one format produces healthier choices more reliably. The summary should reflect that comparison and its result, not just describe calorie labeling in general.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Password security guidance for many years emphasized frequent mandatory password changes as a core defense against unauthorized account access, leading many organizations to require new passwords every few months regardless of any actual security concern. Cybersecurity researchers studying this practice found that frequent forced changes often led users to choose weaker, more predictable passwords or write them down insecurely, since memorizing constantly changing complex passwords proved impractical. Many major technology companies have since changed their guidance to recommend long, unique passwords changed only when there is reason to believe they have been compromised.
options: Frequent Password Changes Confirmed to Strengthen Security
Researchers Finding No Downside to Frequent Password Changes
Companies That Increased the Frequency of Required Changes
Research Showing Frequent Password Changes Can Weaken Security
quests.correctAnswer: Research Showing Frequent Password Changes Can Weaken Security
quests.hint: Notice the original justification for frequent password changes and what researchers actually found about the real-world effect of that practice.
quests.explanation: Long-standing security guidance gets overturned here by showing that the practice it recommended could backfire, leading to weaker security overall. The summary should reflect that reversal rather than confirm the original guidance.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Emergency rooms have traditionally been viewed by hospital administrators primarily as a cost center necessary for handling true medical emergencies, with limited attention paid to non-urgent visits beyond simply redirecting patients elsewhere. A study tracking patients who visited emergency rooms for non-urgent reasons found that many lacked any regular primary care provider at all, using the emergency room as their only consistent point of contact with the healthcare system. Hospitals that responded by connecting these patients with primary care resources during their visit saw a meaningful reduction in repeat non-urgent emergency visits over the following year.
options: Non-Urgent Patients Found to Already Have Primary Care
Hospitals That Refused to Address Non-Urgent Visits
Connecting Patients to Primary Care Reducing Repeat ER Visits
Repeat Visits That Increased After Connecting Patients to Care
quests.correctAnswer: Connecting Patients to Primary Care Reducing Repeat ER Visits
quests.hint: Consider the underlying reason many patients were using the emergency room for non-urgent issues and what intervention actually reduced those repeat visits.
quests.explanation: A gap in primary care access is identified here as the hidden cause behind non-urgent emergency visits, met with a targeted intervention that reduces repeat visits. The summary should connect that root cause with the successful solution.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Streaming platforms have generally assumed that recommendation algorithms work best by showing users more of what they have already watched and enjoyed, reinforcing existing preferences as closely as possible. An internal study at one platform found that users who occasionally received recommendations slightly outside their usual viewing patterns reported higher overall satisfaction with the platform than users who received only closely matched suggestions, even though those same users watched the unusual recommendations less frequently than their typical content. The platform adjusted its algorithm to intentionally include a small percentage of less predictable suggestions.
options: Closely Matched Recommendations Found to Maximize Satisfaction
Unexpected Recommendations Improving Satisfaction Despite Lower Viewing Rates
Users Who Watched Unusual Recommendations More Than Usual Content
A Platform That Removed All Variety from Its Algorithm
quests.correctAnswer: Unexpected Recommendations Improving Satisfaction Despite Lower Viewing Rates
quests.hint: Think about the assumption the platform started with about matching preferences exactly, and notice the surprising gap between how often users watched unusual suggestions and how satisfied they actually felt.
quests.explanation: Satisfaction does not depend simply on how often a recommendation gets watched here, since less-watched unusual suggestions still boost overall satisfaction. The summary should capture that nuanced finding rather than confirm the original assumption about close matching.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Workplace exit interviews have traditionally been conducted by human resources staff immediately before an employee's final day, a practice intended to gather honest feedback about why people choose to leave. Several companies that switched to conducting these interviews with a neutral third party several weeks after departure, once any immediate tension had settled, found that departing employees offered noticeably more detailed and constructive feedback than they had under the original timing and format. This shift has helped some companies identify recurring, previously unspoken concerns across multiple departments.
options: Delayed, Third-Party Interviews Producing More Honest Employee Feedback
Immediate HR Interviews Found to Produce the Most Detail
Departing Employees Who Refused to Give Any Feedback
A Shift That Revealed No New Information for Companies
quests.correctAnswer: Delayed, Third-Party Interviews Producing More Honest Employee Feedback
quests.hint: Look at what made the original exit interview timing and format limited, and what change led to more useful feedback.
quests.explanation: Changing both the timing and the interviewer leads to richer, more honest feedback than the traditional approach. The summary should connect those specific changes with the improved quality of information companies received.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Personal finance advice has traditionally encouraged people to track every single expense in detailed categories as the foundation of good budgeting, an approach many people find tedious enough to abandon within weeks. A study comparing detailed expense tracking with a simpler method, where people only tracked their three largest discretionary spending categories closely while estimating the rest, found that participants using the simpler method sustained their budgeting habit far longer and ultimately saved a comparable amount of money over the course of a year.
options: A Simpler Budgeting Method Proving as Effective as Detailed Tracking
Detailed Tracking Confirmed as the Only Effective Method
Simpler Tracking Found to Save Far Less Money Overall
Participants Who Abandoned the Simpler Method Within Weeks
quests.correctAnswer: A Simpler Budgeting Method Proving as Effective as Detailed Tracking
quests.hint: Ask yourself how the traditional budgeting advice compares with the simpler alternative, in terms of both sustainability and overall results.
quests.explanation: A tedious traditional method is compared here with a simpler alternative, and the simpler one proves just as effective while being easier to maintain. The summary should capture that equivalence in results, not assume detailed tracking was superior.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Standardized testing policy in many regions has long assumed that more frequent testing throughout the school year provides teachers with better, more actionable insight into student progress. A district that reduced its testing frequency by half while extending the depth of feedback provided after each remaining test found that teachers reported feeling more able to adjust instruction meaningfully, compared to when frequent but shallow test data had previously left them with numbers but little clear direction for changing their teaching.
options: More Frequent Testing Confirmed as More Useful for Teachers
Teachers Who Felt Less Able to Adjust Instruction After the Change
Fewer, Deeper Tests Helping Teachers Adjust Instruction More Effectively
A District That Increased Testing Frequency Even Further
quests.correctAnswer: Fewer, Deeper Tests Helping Teachers Adjust Instruction More Effectively
quests.hint: Identify the assumption behind frequent testing and what the district actually found once it reduced frequency but increased the depth of feedback.
quests.explanation: The assumption that more frequent testing automatically helps teachers gets challenged here, showing that fewer but richer assessments were actually more useful. The summary should reflect that finding rather than confirm the value of frequent testing.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Open-plan office layouts became popular partly on the assumption that removing physical walls would naturally increase spontaneous collaboration between employees from different teams. Several long-term workplace studies tracking actual interaction patterns found that face-to-face conversation between coworkers often decreased after the switch to open layouts, as employees turned to digital messaging instead to preserve some sense of privacy in a space lacking it. Some companies have since redesigned their open offices to include small, semi-private spaces intended to restore the in-person collaboration the original layout was supposed to encourage.
options: Open Layouts Confirmed to Boost In-Person Collaboration
Open Offices Reducing, Not Increasing, Face-to-Face Talk
Employees Who Increased Face-to-Face Talk in Open Offices
Companies That Removed All Private Spaces from Their Offices
quests.correctAnswer: Open Offices Reducing, Not Increasing, Face-to-Face Talk
quests.hint: Focus on what open-plan offices were originally designed to encourage and what the long-term studies actually found about how employees behaved in that space.
quests.explanation: The original assumption behind open-plan design is overturned here by showing it often reduced in-person interaction rather than increasing it. The summary should reflect that counterintuitive finding, not confirm the original design goal.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Airlines have traditionally assumed that offering more seating options and add-on fees gives customers valuable flexibility to customize their trip based on individual needs and budget. Customer satisfaction surveys at several airlines, however, found that travelers who faced numerous optional fees during booking reported significantly more decision fatigue and post-purchase regret than travelers who paid a single, slightly higher all-inclusive fare, even when the total cost ended up similar between the two groups. A few airlines have begun testing simplified all-inclusive fare options as a result.
options: Optional Fees Confirmed to Increase Customer Satisfaction
Travelers Who Preferred Numerous Optional Fees Over One Fare
Airlines That Abandoned All-Inclusive Fare Testing Immediately
All-Inclusive Fares Reducing Decision Fatigue Despite Similar Costs
quests.correctAnswer: All-Inclusive Fares Reducing Decision Fatigue Despite Similar Costs
quests.hint: Picture what airlines assumed customers wanted from many small fee choices, and notice what the survey actually revealed about how customers felt, even when total cost was the same.
quests.explanation: Having many small choices creates stress rather than valued flexibility here, even at similar overall prices. The summary should reflect that finding about decision fatigue rather than confirm the assumption about flexibility being preferred.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Family therapists have traditionally encouraged parents experiencing conflict with teenagers to schedule dedicated, structured conversations specifically about the disagreement at hand. Several therapists who tracked outcomes over time found that conversations happening informally during shared activities, like cooking or driving somewhere together, often produced more openness from teenagers than scheduled sit-down talks, possibly because the lack of direct eye contact and explicit framing as 'a serious talk' reduced the teenager's sense of being put on the spot. Some therapists now recommend parents look for these informal moments rather than always scheduling formal conversations.
options: Scheduled Sit-Down Talks Confirmed as Most Effective
Teenagers Found to Prefer Direct Eye Contact During Talks
Therapists Who Stopped Recommending Any Form of Conversation
Informal Moments Outperforming Scheduled Talks for Teen Openness
quests.correctAnswer: Informal Moments Outperforming Scheduled Talks for Teen Openness
quests.hint: Compare the traditional advice for talking with teenagers with what therapists actually found worked better for getting teens to open up.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Retailers have long assumed that placing the most popular, high-demand products near store entrances maximizes sales by capturing customer attention immediately upon arrival. A chain that experimented with moving popular items to the back of stores instead, requiring customers to walk past other merchandise to reach them, found that overall basket size increased, since customers exposed to a wider variety of products along the way added more impulse items to their carts than when popular products were available immediately at the entrance.
options: Entrance Placement Confirmed to Maximize Overall Sales
Customers Who Added Fewer Items After the Layout Change
Moving Popular Items Back Increasing Overall Basket Size
A Chain That Reversed the Experiment Immediately Due to Losses
quests.correctAnswer: Moving Popular Items Back Increasing Overall Basket Size
quests.hint: Weigh the traditional assumption about placing popular items near the entrance against what the experiment with moving them actually revealed about total purchases.
quests.explanation: An assumption about entrance placement maximizing sales gets overturned here, showing that moving popular items elsewhere increased overall purchases through exposure to other products. The summary should reflect that counterintuitive layout finding.
